name: tar
summary: Pack directories into a single archive (optionally compressed), list archives, and unpack them.
compat: Letters: c create, t list, x extract, f archive file name (must be followed by the name), z gzip, J xz, v verbose. GNU and BusyBox tar both auto-detect compression when extracting with just -xf.

examples.title: Create a gzip-compressed archive of a directory
examples.explain: The archive file name comes right after f. Paths inside the archive are stored relative to how you named <dir>.
examples.warning: An existing file with the archive's name is overwritten.

examples.title: List the contents before extracting
examples.explain: Inspect-first: see whether everything is inside one top-level directory or would be scattered into your current directory, and spot absolute or ../ paths.

examples.title: Extract into a chosen directory
examples.explain: -C changes into <dest-dir> (which must exist) before extracting, keeping your current directory tidy.
examples.warning: Files in <dest-dir> with the same paths as archive members are overwritten. Extract unknown archives into a new empty directory.

examples.title: Create an xz-compressed archive
examples.explain: xz compresses better than gzip but is slower. Kernel and many source releases ship as .tar.xz.
examples.warning: An existing file with the archive's name is overwritten.

name: gzip
summary: Compress or decompress single files (.gz); zcat reads them without unpacking.
compat: gzip compresses individual files, not directories; use tar for directories. -k is supported by GNU gzip 1.6+ and BusyBox.

examples.title: Compress a file but keep the original
examples.explain: Creates <file>.gz. Without -k, gzip deletes the original after compressing it.

examples.title: Read a compressed file without unpacking it
examples.explain: Rotated logs (/var/log/*.gz) and the kernel config (/proc/config.gz, when enabled) are gzip files.

examples.title: Decompress
examples.explain: Restores <file> and removes the .gz (add -k to keep it).
examples.warning: Refuses to overwrite an existing <file> unless forced; read the prompt.

name: xz
summary: High-ratio compression for single files (.xz), common for kernel sources and disk images.
compat: -T0 (use all CPU cores) is supported by XZ Utils 5.2+.

examples.title: Decompress a downloaded image, keeping the .xz
examples.explain: -d decompresses, -k keeps the compressed file in case you need it again.

examples.title: Compress using all CPU cores
options: Use as many threads as there are cores

examples.title: Show compressed and uncompressed size
examples.explain: Useful to know how much space an image needs before decompressing it.

name: zip
summary: Create .zip archives, the format most easily opened on Windows and macOS.
compat: zip does not preserve Unix ownership the way tar does; prefer tar for Linux-to-Linux transfers.

examples.title: Zip a directory recursively
examples.explain: -r includes everything below <dir>. If the zip exists, files are added or updated in it.

name: unzip
compat: When a file already exists, unzip asks whether to replace it unless -o (overwrite) or -n (never) is given.

examples.title: List the contents first
examples.explain: Check whether the files sit inside a folder or would be spread into the current directory.

examples.title: Extract into a new directory
examples.explain: -d creates <dest-dir> if needed and extracts there.

name: sha256sum
summary: Compute and verify SHA-256 checksums, to confirm a download or image is intact.
compat: Same usage for md5sum, sha1sum and sha512sum. MD5 and SHA-1 detect accidental corruption but are not secure against deliberate tampering.

examples.title: Print a file's checksum
examples.explain: Compare the 64 hex characters with the value published next to the download.

examples.title: Verify files against a checksum list
examples.explain: Each line of the list is 'hash  filename'. Prints OK or FAILED per file and exits non-zero if any fail. Lines for files you did not download show as missing; add --ignore-missing (GNU) to skip them.
options: Check hashes listed in the file
